description:
Found by defk-ds0 (examples/release_debian on branch defk-ds0/debian-release). Defk.Build writes each kernel .so to _build/<env>/defk/ and the generated __defk_load__ loads it from that absolute build path. mix release does not copy that directory, so a release boots with on_load_function_failed (cannot open shared object file) and the module is undefined. The ds0 Dockerfile works around it by copying _build/prod/defk to the same absolute path in the runtime image.

Fix: write the .so under the owning app's priv/ (as elixir_make packages do) and load it via :code.priv_dir/1 (or Application.app_dir) at load time, so it travels with the release and survives relocation. Keep the content-hash cache behaviour.

Done when the ds0 Dockerfile builds and runs with COPY_SO=0 (no manual copy), a test checks the load path is relative to the app's priv dir, and examples/release_debian/README.md drops the workaround.

comments.text: The HexDocs cold test (defk-djy.9) hit this from the docs side: getting-started said the runtime needs no compiler without the release caveat, and the workaround lived only in examples/release_debian on GitHub. defk-djy.9 added the caveat to getting-started and put the workaround steps (same absolute path, a sketch Dockerfile, the __defk_lib__/0 check) in docs/guides/deploying.md. When this ticket lands, remove both.

From defk-fr7 (2026-10-11): __defk_lib__/0 (lib/defk.ex ~345) compiles the absolute .so path into the beam, so a moved project with stale beams, or a release run from another path, points at the old .so. Relevant to shipping .so files in releases.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Kernel shared libraries travel with the owning app (its priv dir) and load relative to it, so `mix release` and relocated builds work without copying `_build/<env>/defk`

**Current behavior:**
`Defk.Build` writes each kernel library to `_build/<env>/defk/<Module>-<key>.so` and the generated `__defk_load__/0` and `__defk_lib__/0` compile that absolute path into the module. `mix release` does not copy that directory, so a release boots with `on_load_function_failed` (cannot open shared object file); a release or project moved to another path points at the old file. examples/release_debian (Dockerfile `COPY_SO`) and docs/guides/deploying.md + getting-started work around it by copying the directory to the same absolute path. Confirmed during triage from the code path.

**Desired behavior:**
- When the kernel module belongs to a Mix app, its library is placed under that app's priv directory (in the build output, so it ships in releases) and `__defk_load__/0` resolves the path at load time from the app (`:code.priv_dir/1` or `Application.app_dir/2`), not from a compile-time absolute path. `__defk_lib__/0` reports the resolved path.
- Must not write generated libraries into the project's source `priv/`: in dev `_build/<env>/lib/<app>/priv` is a symlink to the source `priv/`, so pick a location that ships with the release without polluting the source tree (or, if that is unavoidable, a dedicated ignored subdirectory, justified in the commit and docs).
- Code with no owning Mix app (scripts, `Mix.install`, `Code.compile_string`) keeps today's behaviour (absolute build path).
- The content-hash cache (`Defk.Build` cache key, reuse of an unchanged build, the `.remarks` cache) keeps working, including for apps that are dependencies of another project.

**Key interfaces:**
- Generated `__defk_load__/0` (`:erlang.load_nif/2` path) and `__defk_lib__/0`
- `Defk.Build` output location and cache lookup
- docs: deploying guide, getting-started release caveat, `docs/language.md` build-output notes, ADR-0006 row "Build output `_build/<env>/defk/...`"

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A test builds a release-like layout (or moves the compiled app's ebin/priv to another directory) and the kernel module loads and runs from there without the original `_build/<env>/defk`
- [ ] A test checks the load path is relative to the app's priv dir for an app module, and absolute for a script module
- [ ] An unchanged kernel is not recompiled on a second build (cache still hits)
- [ ] The source `priv/` gains no generated files after `mix test` (or only an ignored subdirectory, as decided above)
- [ ] examples/release_debian Dockerfile/README, docs/guides/deploying.md and getting-started drop the copy workaround
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean
- [ ] Note in the report that the Docker build with `COPY_SO=0` was NOT run (no Docker on this machine); the maintainer verifies it

**Out of scope:**
- Architecture-specific builds or shipping several builds per kernel (defk-ulk.3)
- Precompiled libraries for Hex packages (elixir_make-style downloads)
- Changing the cache key contents

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

**Brief amendment (2026-10-11):** Podman is available here (`podman`, machine podman-machine-default, linux/arm64, running). Replace the criterion 'Note that the Docker build with COPY_SO=0 was NOT run' with:

- [ ] `podman build` of examples/release_debian with COPY_SO=0 (no manual copy of _build/<env>/defk) succeeds, and running the image calls a kernel successfully; report the commands and output. If the Dockerfile relies on Docker-only features, adapt it so it builds with both.
Decision (2026-10-12): kernel libraries in the app's ebin/ (not priv/) are accepted.

title: Ship kernel .so files in mix releases
